usage.callShape: POST https://stablephone.dev/api/lookup with JSON body {phone_number} (E.164) → 202 {token}; then poll GET https://stablephone.dev/api/lookup/status?token=<jwt> with SIWX (paying wallet, free) until body.status=="complete"
usage.outputShape: Status poll body: body.status ("complete"), body.imessage, body.facetime (available|unavailable|unknown), body.carrier, body.country, body.checked_at. (POST response: body.token JWT)
quirks: Two-step async: paid POST /api/lookup returns HTTP 202 with {token} (a JWT), NOT the result. The actual result comes from the status endpoint.

Poll GET /api/lookup/status?token=<jwt> with SIWX auth (same paying wallet), which is FREE. In this run status was 'complete' on the first poll (~0s), but spec says it can take 30-90s — poll every 3-5s.
Token (JWT) expires after 60 min; iat/exp embedded. Re-querying the same number within ~1h reuses cached result (no extra charge).
imessage/facetime values are available|unavailable|unknown (unknown ~ landline/VoIP). For test number +14155551234 both returned 'unavailable' and carrier/country were null.
Status endpoint requires SIWX sign-in (paying wallet identity), not x402 payment — pass it as the SIWX-authed GET.
usage.guide: Check whether a phone number has iMessage/FaceTime plus carrier/country. POST https://stablephone.dev/api/lookup with {"phone_number":"+1..."} in E.164 — this pays $0.05 USDC on Base via x402 and returns HTTP 202 {token} (a JWT), not the answer. Then poll GET https://stablephone.dev/api/lookup/status?token=<jwt> using SIWX (the same paying wallet, free) every 3-5s until body.status=="complete" (typically 0-90s; the JWT is valid 60 min). Read body.imessage / body.facetime (available|unavailable|unknown) plus body.carrier and body.country.
